papers.title: Tailoring Ti-6Al-4V during additive manufacturing with in situ sulphur microadditions to enhance machinability
papers.abstract: Improving the machinability of titanium alloys remains a major barrier in aerospace manufacturing, particularly for additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V components that exhibit heterogeneous microstructures and high cutting resistance. This study introduces a new alloy modification machinability enhancement strategy by incorporating trace sulphur (<300ppm) via MoS₂ during wire-based directed energy deposition (W-DED). The modified alloy meets the composition requirements of Ti-6Al-4V ELI (ASTM Grade 23) titanium and retains its structural integrity while developing sulphur-rich particles at the grain boundary that act as low-strength shear paths and facilitate plastic flow during cutting. Machinability improvements include an approximate 8% reduction in average cutting forces (F r ) and a th r eefold decrease in tool flank wear compared to the unmodified alloy. Additionally, there was a noticeable change in chip morphology, shifting from distinctly serrated to more continuous. Machining trials show lower cutting forces, delayed crater and flank wear, and a shift in chip morphology from distinctly serrated to more continuous. This behaviour parallels the classical free-cutting effect of sulphur in steels yet is demonstrated here for the first time in an additively manufactured titanium alloy system. This work establishes in-process sulphur micro-addition as an effective pathway for tailoring the machining response of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V, offering a practical route for producing difficult-to-cut aerospace components with improved manufacturing efficiency. • Trace sulphur added to Ti-6Al-4V via W-DED without affecting mechanical properties • Sulphur precipitates at prior-β grain boundaries, forming particles that ease machining • Cutting forces drop ~8%, with crater and flank wear greatly reduced • Chip morphology shifts to continuous, aided by higher shear angle and less segmentation • Up-milling roughness improves from 3.16 µm to 0.71 µm due to stable chip formation

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文是关于增材制造过程中原位添加硫以改善切削加工性，而非后处理工艺对疲劳性能的影响。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not involve any post-processing treatment; instead it modifies the alloy composition in situ during additive manufacturing, and its focus is on machinability rather than fatigue or mechanical performance improvement via post-processing.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的切削加工性以降低制造成本
summary_zh.method: 在W-DED过程中添加微量MoS₂引入硫元素，形成晶界硫化物促进剪切
summary_zh.result: 切削力降低约8%，刀具磨损减少三倍，切屑形态由锯齿状变为连续状
summary_zh.validation: 通过切削力测量、刀具磨损分析和切屑形貌表征验证

summary_en.motivation: To improve the machinability of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V by introducing a free-cutting effect similar to sulfur in steels.
summary_en.method: Trace sulfur was added via MoS₂ during wire-based directed energy deposition, forming sulfur-rich particles at grain boundaries that act as low-strength shear paths.
summary_en.result: Average cutting forces dropped by approximately 8% and tool flank wear was reduced threefold, with chip morphology shifting from serrated to continuous.
summary_en.validation: Experimental machining trials including cutting force measurements, flank wear analysis, and chip morphology characterization were performed.

papers.title: Effects of heat treatment temperature and time on the fitness accuracy, retentive force, and permanent deformation of selective laser melting Ti-6Al-4V clasps
papers.abstract: The selective laser melting (SLM) technology of Ti-6Al-4V (TC4) demonstrates significant advantages in fabricating clasps for removable partial dentures, whereas subsequent heat treatment plays a crucial role in performance optimization. This study systematically investigated the effects of heat treatment temperature and time on the fitness accuracy, retentive force, and permanent deformation of SLM TC4 clasps. TC4 clasp specimens were manufactured using SLM technology and subjected to heat treatment under different temperatures (700, 750, 800, and 850℃) and times (0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 h). The fitness accuracy, retentive force, and permanent deformation after 10,000 insertion/removal cycles were measured for each group and statistically analyzed. The results revealed that the 700℃/0.5 h group showed significantly reduced fitness accuracy. After cyclic testing, the retentive force of all groups decreased by 4.06%&ndash;12.18%, with heat treatment temperature significantly affecting both initial and final retentive forces. The time of heat treatment demonstrated no substantial influence. The permanent deformation of the clasps (31.15&ndash;38.05 &mu;m) remained unaffected by variations in either heat treatment temperature or time. Based on overall performance, the 700℃/0.5 h heat treatment condition is not recommended. Instead, selecting shorter time protocols such as 0.5 h within the 750℃&ndash;850℃ range can help enhance production efficiency while maintaining performance standards.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文研究热处理对SLM Ti-6Al-4V卡环的力学性能影响，但专注于牙科应用，而非通用疲劳性能。
llm.why_not_core: Does not investigate microstructure evolution, porosity closure, or conventional tensile/fatigue properties; application-specific to dental clasps.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究热处理温度和时间对SLM Ti-6Al-4V卡环性能的影响。
summary_zh.method: 制备SLM TC4卡环，在不同温度和时间下热处理后测量精度、固位力和永久变形。
summary_zh.result: 700°C/0.5h组精度显著下降，固位力下降4-12%，永久变形约31-38 μm且不受热处理影响。
summary_zh.validation: 通过10,000次插入/移除循环测试验证性能。

summary_en.motivation: This study investigates the effects of heat treatment temperature and time on the performance of SLM Ti-6Al-4V dental clasps.
summary_en.method: Ti-6Al-4V clasps were fabricated by SLM and heat-treated at various temperatures (700-850°C) and times (0.5-1.5 h), then tested for fitness accuracy, retentive force, and permanent deformation.
summary_en.result: The 700°C/0.5 h group exhibited significantly reduced accuracy; retentive force decreased by 4.06-12.18% after 10,000 cycles, while permanent deformation (31.15-38.05 μm) was unaffected by heat treatment parameters.
summary_en.validation: Cyclic insertion/removal testing was performed to simulate clinical use and measure performance changes.
